definitions.explanation: A fence made of wooden boards or planks arranged vertically or horizontally. A traditional form of property enclosure, less ornamental than other Japanese fence types.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}を{板垣|いたがき}で{囲|かこ}んだ。
examples.english: I enclosed the garden with a plank fence.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{板垣|いたがき}が{台風|たいふう}で{倒|たお}れた。
examples.english: The old plank fence fell over in the typhoon.

examples.japanese: {隣家|りんか}との{境|さかい}に{板垣|いたがき}を{新|あたら}しく{立|た}て{直|なお}した。
examples.english: We rebuilt the plank fence on the boundary with the neighboring house.

notes:
{板|いた} (board, plank) + {垣|かき} (fence, hedge), with rendaku changing かき to がき. One of several traditional fence types in Japanese architecture.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生|い}け{垣|がき}: living hedge made of plants — uses plants instead of wood
- {竹垣|たけがき}: bamboo fence — uses bamboo poles, more decorative
- {塀|へい}: wall, solid fence — sturdier, often masonry or thick wood
- {柵|さく}: fence, railing — usually open structure with bars or slats

NOTE: {板垣|いたがき} is also a common Japanese surname, most famously borne by {板垣|いたがき} {退助|たいすけ} (1837–1919), a prominent Meiji-era politician.
